description: A composite of eight secondary-electron SEM micrographs of fatigue fracture surfaces, arranged in two rows of four with panel letters (a)-(h). Every panel consists of a low-magnification overview of the fatigue crack propagation zone, each carrying its own 100 μm scale bar, plus a magnified inset boxed in cyan (a small cyan box in the overview marks the imaged region) with its own 10 μm scale bar showing fatigue striations. According to the caption the top row (a-d) is at a stress amplitude of 180 MPa and the bottom row (e-h) at 315 MPa; within each row the panels correspond, left to right, to samples ST (a,e), 550-6 (b,f), 600-6 (c,g) and 650-6 (d,h). All overviews show rough, faceted transgranular fracture topography with tear ridges and secondary cracking; no grain-boundary facets are evident. The insets are the informative part: (a) shows sparse, widely spaced striations; (b) shows dense, fine, closely spaced parallel striations; (c) shows fine striations crossed by a fan-like vein pattern; (d) shows predominantly striated terrain; (e) shows wavy, widely spaced striations; (f) shows fine closely spaced striations; (g) shows dense parallel striations; (h) shows rougher, more coarsely spaced striations. Collectively the figure shows that all samples fail by transgranular, striation-forming fatigue crack growth, with the finest striation spacing in the 550-6 and 600-6 conditions, which the citing text links to their longer fatigue lives. No numeric spacing values are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: The figure is an 8-panel composite of SEM fracture-surface micrographs, each with a 100 μm scale-bar overview plus a cyan-boxed magnified inset carrying a 10 μm scale bar.
The caption states the top row (a-d) corresponds to a stress amplitude of 180 MPa and the bottom row (e-h) to 315 MPa.
The caption assigns the panels column-wise to samples ST (a,e), 550-6 (b,f), 600-6 (c,g) and 650-6 (d,h).
Well-defined fatigue striations are visible in the magnified insets of all eight panels, indicating transgranular crack advancement.
The inset of panel (b) (550-6, 180 MPa) shows the finest and most closely spaced parallel striations among the 180 MPa group.
The citing text states the narrowest striation spacing occurs in the 550-6 sample at 315 MPa and in the 600-6 sample at 180 MPa.
The citing text links the reduced striation spacing of 550-6 and 600-6 to their longer fatigue lives shown in Fig. 5.
The overview micrographs show rough, faceted transgranular fracture topography with tear ridges and secondary cracking; no intergranular facets are apparent.
The inset of panel (c) (600-6, 180 MPa) shows fine striations overprinted by a fan-like vein pattern.
The insets of panels (a) and (e) (sample ST) show the most widely spaced and least regular striations of the 180 MPa and 315 MPa groups respectively.
No numeric striation-spacing values are printed on any panel of the figure.
